questions.q: What did Lessons 50-52 build up, over the course of those three lessons?
options: Retrieval-augmented generation, from the concept, to a vector index over a data catalog, to an actual RAG pipeline over Fabric metadata
A full Copilot installation guide for Microsoft Fabric
A guide to writing KQL queries from scratch
The chapter's guardrails on what not to hand an LLM
questions.explain: Lesson 50 explained RAG, Lesson 51 built a vector index over a catalog, and Lesson 52 built an actual pipeline over Fabric metadata.

questions.q: What single pattern repeats across Lessons 53, 54, and 55 (test generation, RCA drafting, and schema mapping)?
options: Draft with the LLM, then verify the output against something real before it's trusted or shipped
Skip verification since the AI's output is always accurate
Each lesson uses a completely unrelated approach with no common pattern
Only ship the AI's first draft without any review step
questions.explain: Every one of those three lessons ends the same way: draft, then check against something real.

questions.q: Why does Lesson 56's guardrails lesson exist, in relation to the draft-then-verify pattern from Lessons 53-55?
options: It draws the hard line on what should never enter a prompt in the first place, and reminds engineers that shipping an AI-assisted draft is still their responsibility
It exists to replace the verification step entirely
It has no real connection to the earlier lessons in the chapter
It only applies to schema mapping, not test generation or RCA drafting
questions.explain: Guardrails protect the draft-then-verify pattern by keeping sensitive data out of prompts and keeping responsibility with the engineer.

questions.q: How does Lesson 60 connect this chapter back to Fabric & Real-Time Analytics's production chapter?
options: It frames AI as one more tool inside the existing production toolkit (testing, observability, incident response, governance), not a replacement for any of those practices
It argues AI has made the entire production chapter obsolete
It has no connection to the earlier course at all
It claims AI can now make all SLA and incident-resolution decisions independently
questions.explain: Lesson 60's explicit point is that AI speeds up tasks within established production practices without replacing the practices or the judgment behind them.

questions.q: What comes immediately after Chapter 3 in this course, and what does it cover?
options: Chapter 4, "Added Projects — Capstones," with three mini-capstone projects applying the whole four-course track
A second AI chapter covering even more advanced LLM techniques
A return to Chapter 1's system design topics with no new material
The end of the course, with no further chapters
questions.explain: Chapter 3 is now complete; Chapter 4 puts system design, DP-700, and this AI chapter into practice on real end-to-end builds.
